No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

Rakhigarhi, in Hisar district of Haryana, is one of the largest settlements of the Harappan civilisation. An archaeologist walks you through the mounds and the published evidence for its streets, crafts, drains and burials, and a local host shows you the village that stands beside them today.

The day is designed to be worth the journey even when no trench is open and the museum is closed. A visit to a live excavation or a gallery can be added only when it is confirmed for your date.

Transport from Delhi, the start time, meals and pace are arranged with you, and the quotation states exactly what is included.

What it covers

  • The mounds and what excavation has found in them
  • Published finds, pottery and burials, with reproductions
  • Lunch with a local host
  • The village today, in conversation with the people who live there

How the time is spent

  1. Arrival and briefing 35 min

    What a mound is, where Rakhigarhi sits in the Harappan story, and how to behave on a protected site.

  2. The archaeological landscape 75 min

    The accessible parts of selected mounds, read against the published evidence for streets, craft areas, drains and burial grounds.

    You: annotate a site map in your field notebook

  3. Finds and methods 45 min

    Excavation photographs, pottery types and burials, with reproductions: what each tells us and what it does not.

    You: sort evidence from reconstruction

  4. Lunch 60 min

    A meal arranged with a local host, or a restaurant or packed lunch. Dietary needs are confirmed when you book.

  5. The village today 65 min

    A walk or a conversation about food and crafts, led by a local host who has agreed to it. No uninvited visits, and photographs only with permission.

  6. Wrap-up 30 min

    The ancient city and the present village as two different histories, your questions, and options for a second day.

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Describe major archaeological questions at Rakhigarhi using published excavation results.
  • Compare material evidence and reconstructions rather than treating all hypotheses as settled.
  • Engage respectfully with living local culture without claiming simple direct continuity from ancient Harappans.

You take away

A field journal and a comparison sheet from the day.

Options you can add

  • A live excavation. Only when a dig is under way on your date and the site team agrees to a supervised visit.
  • A museum or interpretation centre. Only if it is open on your date; otherwise a printed research pack.
  • A pottery and craft demonstration. With a craftsperson, quoted for your group.
  • A research seminar. With a scholar, for college and research groups.
  • A photography and field-recording workshop. With permission for every photograph taken.
  • An overnight stay. A resort, hotel or heritage lodging nearby, quoted by room. Some lodgings have age rules for school groups.
  • A second day nearby. Hisar, Hansi or Agroha, or a seminar comparing Harappan sites.

Good to know

  • Travel time from Delhi is added at both ends of the day and depends on where you start.
  • We never promise an open trench or a find. The day is planned to be worthwhile without them.
  • We do not claim that the people of the village today descend directly from the Harappans. The two histories are told separately.
